Treatment summary
Patient presented following a rear-end mootr vehicle collision with complaints of neck
pain, stiffness, and headache. Over the course of twenty visits, care consisted of
supervised physical therapy, range-of-motion exercises, manual therapy, and home
exercise instruction. Cervical examination revealed reduced range of motion and
parasipnal muscle tenderness consistent with soft tissue injury, while cretain
neurological screening tests, including reflexes, strength, and sensation, returned
normal results. The mechanism and force of the collision align well with the injury
pattern described. No prior injury or treatment involving the cervical spine is known.
Treatment followed a typiacl progression, with visit frequency decreasing as symptoms
improved and range of motion returned closer to baseline. Billing records reflect
single charges for each service rendered, with no duplicated entries. Patient was
discharged to self-directed home exercise with instructions to return if symptoms
recur.
</page>

Rate each feature below that THIS page gives evidence about. Leave out a feature the page

- objective_support: Do objective tests (imaging, exam findings) support the complaints? Allowed: Strong, Partial, Predominantly subjective, Contradicted.
- pre_existing_condition: Did an earlier condition of the same body area add to the complaints? Allowed: None, Minor, Material, Predominant.
- duplicate_billing: Was the same service, visit or part billed twice? Allowed: None, Possible, Confirmed.
